chunks: "In the Tawrah, it is written that: My houses on the earth are the mosques; so glad tidings to a servant who purifies himself in his house, then visits Me in My house. Indeed, honoring the visitor is incumbent upon the one visited. Indeed, give glad tidings to those who walk in the darkness to the mosques of a radiant light on the Day of Judgment."

key_terms.التَّوْرَاةِ: the Tawrah, cited here as containing this sacred teaching
key_terms.الظُّلُمَاتِ: the darknesses, meaning the dark times of night or low light
key_terms.النُّورِ السَّاطِعِ: radiant light, the promised illumination on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْمَزُورِ: the one visited, here referring to Allah by way of honoring His house
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدُ: the mosques, the places of worship on earth
key_terms.بُيُوتِي: My houses, referring to places Allah has specially honored
key_terms.تَطَهَّرَ: purified himself, meaning he attained ritual cleanliness before going
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, the day of resurrection and final reckoning

ai.seo_question: What reward is mentioned for those who walk to the mosques in darkness?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the sanctity of mosques as houses attributed to Allah and encourages believers to come to them in a state of taharah (ritual purity). It also promises a great reward in the afterlife for those who go to the mosques in darkness, describing their recompense as radiant light on the Day of Judgment.
